daytona-shim: Daytona Championship USA without TeknoParrot
===========================================================

Status: test build. 2019 and 2017 run on the Steam Deck. New and untested:
PlayStation / Switch pads, wheels and force feedback (SDL3).

Install
-------
Copy everything in this folder (DaytonaLauncher.exe, dinput8.dll, SDL3.dll
and shim.ini) into the folder that holds Daytona.exe:

    ...\Sega\Daytona\dinput8.dll      (2019)
    ...\Daytona\dinput8.dll            (2017)

2017: keep Daytona.exe.original next to Daytona.exe. The Daytona.exe in
that folder is TeknoParrot's patched copy; the shim reads the original and
puts its code back in memory, so you start Daytona.exe as usual. Neither
file is changed.

To remove it, delete those files again. The shim itself changes nothing in
the game folder; the launcher changes the game's own settings files only
when you save, and keeps the first version of each as .shim-backup. Close TeknoParrot first (its shell takes the same port).

The launcher
------------
On the Steam Deck (and anywhere under Proton) DaytonaLauncher.exe opens full
screen, made for a controller: the title with START and OPTIONS, and one
list of the game's settings. D-pad or left stick to move, left / right to
change a setting, A (Cross on PlayStation) to select, B (Circle) to go back.
On a keyboard: arrows, Enter, Esc or Backspace. Settings are saved when you
leave the list. The button prompts follow the pad you use. It fills the
screen at its own resolution: 1280x800 on the Deck, 1920x1080 (or any
other size) elsewhere.

CONTROLS on the title screen sets up the pad and wheel for the chosen
edition (its shim.ini): every action of the pad, the wheel's axes and
buttons, steering scale, pedals, and force feedback / rumble strength.
Left / right goes through the choices; A (Cross) on a pad action or a
wheel axis or button waits for you to press the button, or move the stick,
trigger, wheel or pedal, that you want (Esc on the keyboard cancels). The
top of the screen shows what the game will get from your wheel.

Both editions from one launcher: with the 2017 and 2019 games both
installed, the edition under the logo is a choice (left / right). START
runs that edition and OPTIONS edits its settings; the launcher remembers
the last one. Copy dinput8.dll, SDL3.dll and shim.ini next to each
edition's Daytona.exe; one launcher (and one Steam shortcut) is enough.
The launcher finds the other edition in the folders around its own (for
example Games/Daytona 2019/Sega/Daytona and Games/Daytona 2017/Daytona).
If it does not, name the folders that hold each Daytona.exe in a
launcher.ini beside the launcher:
    [Editions]
    2017=Z:\home\deck\Games\Daytona 2017\Daytona
    2019=Z:\home\deck\Games\Daytona 2019\Sega\Daytona

On Windows it opens as a window with tabs:
  Game        free play, music / effects / voice volume (ShellData.ini)
  Rules       difficulty, race length, car and track select, tournament
              and the other operator settings (GameSettings.ini)
  Controller  the pad layout; Detect, then press the button you want
  Wheel       axes, buttons (Detect works for these too), steering scale,
              pedals, force feedback and rumble strength; a live readout
              shows what the game will get from your wheel
  Play        saves, starts Daytona.exe, and closes when the game does
Options: --play starts the game at once (the edition chosen last), --big opens the full-screen
launcher on Windows, --desktop the window under Proton. 

Run on Windows
--------------
Double-click DaytonaLauncher.exe (or Daytona.exe itself: Windows loads the
dinput8.dll beside it either way).

Run on the Steam Deck (Desktop Mode)
-------------------------------------
1. Steam > Games > Add a Non-Steam Game to My Library > Browse, pick
   DaytonaLauncher.exe (set the file type filter to "All Files" if it is
   hidden).
2. In the new entry's Properties:
   - Compatibility: tick "Force the use of a specific Steam Play
     compatibility tool", choose Proton Experimental (or 9 or later).
   - Launch Options:
         WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b" %command%
     Without this Proton uses its own dinput8 and the shim is not loaded.
     To skip the launcher's window and start racing at once:
         WINEDLLOVERRIDES="dinput8=n,b" %command% --play
   - Start In: the folder holding Daytona.exe (Steam fills it in).
3. Launch it.

If Steam calls the game "Spacewar" and uses that game's controller layout,
a steam_appid.txt (app 480, from another package) is in the game folder.
Delete it (and steam_api.dll or a steam_settings folder if present).

Controls
--------
Controllers: Xbox, PlayStation, Switch and other pads (through SDL3.dll),
and the Deck's own controls through Steam Input. By button position:
  Steering        left stick
  Gas / brake     right / left trigger
  Start           Start / Options / +
  Coin            Back / Share / -
  Shift up/down   right / left bumper
  Views 1-4       top / left / right / bottom button (Xbox: Y / X / B / A)
  Quit            hold Start + Back for a second
Several controllers at once are combined.

Steering wheels (Windows): Logitech, Thrustmaster, Fanatec and other wheels
SDL knows are used by themselves. The defaults suit a Logitech G29 / G923:
paddles shift, Options is Start, Share is Coin, the H-shifter's gears 1-4.
For another wheel, shim.log lists "axis N moved" and "button N pressed" as
you use it; put those numbers in shim.ini [Wheel]. If the wheel turns too
far for full lock, set about 270 degrees in its software or raise
SteeringScale.

Force feedback: the game's own force feedback (what drove the cabinet's
motor) goes to the wheel as a constant force, and to pads as rumble. Set
the strength, or turn it off, in shim.ini [ForceFeedback]; Invert=1 if the
wheel pulls the wrong way.
Keyboard: arrows (steer, gas, brake), Enter start, 5 coin, A / Z shift,
F1-F4 views, Esc quits.

Free play is on by default (ShellData\ShellData.ini, [Credit] Freeplay=1).

If something goes wrong
-----------------------
The shim writes shim.log next to Daytona.exe. Please send it along with
what happened. A good first run shows, in this order:
  hook WS2_32.dll!#4 ... (and the other hooks)
  shell: listening on 127.0.0.1:18888
  shell: game connected
  shell: <- 0x.. / shell: -> 0x2C (the greeting)
  pad: SDL 3.x.x, then "pad: <name> connected as a pad / wheel"
  CreateProcessA(c:\sega\shell\InpWrapper.exe ...): the shim is the force-feedback helper
  ffb: registered with the game window: yes
  (2017) restore: ... ranges (... bytes) put back from Daytona.exe.original, 0 skipped
  dinput: CreateDevice(SEGA IO Controller)
  shell: <- 0x2A (... challenge) every 10 s, each answered with -> 0x2E

If SDL causes trouble (a pad missing or doubled), SDL=0 in shim.ini goes
back to XInput pads only.
